# cu29::simulation - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cu29/1.0.0/cu29/simulation/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#cu29simulation-module)`cu29::simulation` Module

The `cu29::simulation` module provides an interface to simulate tasks in Copper-based systems.
It offers structures, traits, and enums that enable hooking into the lifecycle of tasks, adapting
their behavior, and integrating them with simulated hardware environments.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

This module is specifically designed to manage the lifecycle of tasks during simulation, allowing users to override specific simulation steps and simulate sensor data or hardware interaction using placeholders for real drivers. It includes the following components:

- `CuTaskCallbackState`
- `SimOverride`

[§](https://docs.rs#hooking-simulation-events)Hooking Simulation Events

You can control and simulate task behavior using a callback mechanism. A task in the Copper framework has a lifecycle, and for each stage of the lifecycle, a corresponding callback state is passed to the simulation. This allows you to inject custom logic for each task stage.

[§](https://docs.rs#cutaskcallbackstate-enum)`CuTaskCallbackState` Enum

The `CuTaskCallbackState` enum represents different stages in the lifecycle of a Copper task during a simulation:

- `New(Option<ComponentConfig>)`
- `Start`
- `Preprocess`
- `Process(I, O)`- `I`) and output (- `O`) of the task. For source tasks,- `I`is- `CuMsg<()>`, and for sink tasks,- `O`is- `CuMsg<()>`.
- `Postprocess`
- `Stop`

[§](https://docs.rs#example-usage-callback)Example Usage: Callback

You can combine the expressiveness of the enum matching to intercept and override the task lifecycle for the simulation.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
let mut sim_callback = move |step: SimStep<'_>| -> SimOverride {
    match step {
        // Handle the creation of source tasks, potentially adapting the simulation based on configuration
        SimStep::SourceTask(CuTaskCallbackState::New(Some(config))) => {
            println!("Creating Source Task with configuration: {:?}", config);
            // You can adapt the simulation using the configuration here
            SimOverride::ExecuteByRuntime
        }
        SimStep::SourceTask(CuTaskCallbackState::New(None)) => {
            println!("Creating Source Task without configuration.");
            SimOverride::ExecuteByRuntime
        }
        // Handle the processing step for sink tasks, simulating the response
        SimStep::SinkTask(CuTaskCallbackState::Process(input, output)) => {
            println!("Processing Sink Task...");
            println!("Received input: {:?}", input);
            // Simulate a response by setting the output payload
            output.set_payload(your_simulated_response());
            println!("Set simulated output for Sink Task.");
            SimOverride::ExecutedBySim
        }
        // Generic handling for other phases like Start, Preprocess, Postprocess, or Stop
        SimStep::SourceTask(CuTaskCallbackState::Start)
        | SimStep::SinkTask(CuTaskCallbackState::Start) => {
            println!("Task started.");
            SimOverride::ExecuteByRuntime
        }
        SimStep::SourceTask(CuTaskCallbackState::Stop)
        | SimStep::SinkTask(CuTaskCallbackState::Stop) => {
            println!("Task stopped.");
            SimOverride::ExecuteByRuntime
        }
        // Default fallback for any unhandled cases
        _ => {
            println!("Unhandled simulation step: {:?}", step);
            SimOverride::ExecuteByRuntime
        }
    }
};
```
In this example, `example_callback` is a function that matches against the current step in the simulation and
determines if the simulation should handle it (`SimOverride::ExecutedBySim`) or defer to the runtime’s real
implementation (`SimOverride::ExecuteByRuntime`).

[§](https://docs.rs#task-simulation-with-cusimsrctask-and-cusimsinktask)Task Simulation with `CuSimSrcTask` and `CuSimSinkTask`

The module provides placeholder tasks for source and sink tasks, which do not interact with real hardware but instead simulate the presence of it.

-
`CuSimSrcTask<T>`
-
`CuSimSinkTask<T>`

[§](https://docs.rs#controlling-simulation-flow-simoverride-enum)Controlling Simulation Flow: `SimOverride` Enum

The `SimOverride` enum is used to control how the simulator should proceed at each step. This allows
for fine-grained control of task behavior in the simulation context:

- `ExecutedBySim`
- `ExecuteByRuntime`

[§](https://docs.rs#recorded-replay-helpers)Recorded Replay Helpers

Simulation-enabled generated runtimes expose two recorded replay callbacks:

- `recorded_replay_step`is exact-output replay. It copies recorded outputs from a CopperList and skips the runtime implementation for deterministic log reproduction.
- `recorded_debug_replay_step`is debugger state replay. It injects recorded external inputs, suppresses external side effects, and lets regular Copper tasks execute so restored keyframe state advances to the inspected CL.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [CuNo](https://docs.rs/struct.CuNoBridgeChannels.html)- Bridge - Channels
- Empty channel set used when a simulated bridge has no channel on one side.
- [CuSim](https://docs.rs/struct.CuSimBridge.html)- Bridge
- Placeholder bridge used in simulation when a bridge is configured with
`run_in_sim: false`.
- [CuSim](https://docs.rs/struct.CuSimSinkTask.html)- Sink - Task
- This is a placeholder task for a sink task for the simulations. It basically does nothing in place of a real driver so it won’t try to initialize any hardware.
- [CuSim](https://docs.rs/struct.CuSimSrcTask.html)- SrcTask
- This is a placeholder task for a source task for the simulations. It basically does nothing in place of a real driver so it won’t try to initialize any hardware.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [CuBridge](https://docs.rs/enum.CuBridgeLifecycleState.html)- Lifecycle - State
- Lifecycle callbacks for bridges when running in simulation.
- [CuNo](https://docs.rs/enum.CuNoBridgeChannelId.html)- Bridge - Channel - Id
- Empty channel-id enum used when a simulated bridge has no channel on one side.
- [CuTask](https://docs.rs/enum.CuTaskCallbackState.html)- Callback - State
- This is the state that will be passed to the simulation support to hook into the lifecycle of the tasks.
- [SimOverride](https://docs.rs/enum.SimOverride.html)
- This is the answer the simulator can give to control the simulation flow.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [CuSim](https://docs.rs/trait.CuSimSinkInput.html)- Sink - Input
- Helper to map a payload type (or tuple of payload types) to the corresponding `input_msg!`form.

- Returns the earliest recorded `process_time.start`found in a CopperList.

# cu29::thread_pool - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cu29/1.0.0/cu29/thread_pool/index.html

## Expand description

Construction of configured worker thread pools (std-only).

A pool is built from a [ ThreadPoolConfig](https://docs.rs/prelude/struct.ThreadPoolConfig.html) into a rayon

[whose worker threads optionally get:](https://docs.rs/rayon-core/1.13.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/rayon_core/thread_pool/struct.ThreadPool.html)

`ThreadPool`- a fixed CPU affinity, applied **Spread**: worker`i`is pinned to`affinity[i % affinity.len()]`, so`threads == affinity.len()`yields one worker pinned per dedicated core; and
- a scheduling policy/priority (normal/niceness or `SCHED_FIFO`/`SCHED_RR`).

Affinity and scheduling are applied **once per worker thread at startup**
(never on the per-CopperList hot path), and only when the `rt-scheduling`
feature is enabled on a supported platform (Linux for real-time policies; CPU
affinity is cross-platform). When the feature is off, the requested affinity
and policy are ignored and a warning is emitted.

Per-pool [ OnError](https://docs.rs/prelude/enum.OnError.html) controls what happens when a request cannot be applied
(for example, setting a real-time priority without

`CAP_SYS_NICE`):
[logs and continues with default scheduling, while](https://docs.rs/prelude/enum.OnError.html#variant.Warn)

`OnError::Warn`[fails the build.](https://docs.rs/prelude/enum.OnError.html#variant.Strict)

`OnError::Strict`## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [apply_](https://docs.rs/fn.apply_current_thread_scheduling.html)- current_ - thread_ - scheduling
- [build_](https://docs.rs/fn.build_pool.html)- pool
- Builds a rayon thread pool from a declarative `ThreadPoolConfig`

A bridge behaves similarly to set of [ crate::cutask::CuSrcTask](https://docs.rs/trait.CuSrcTask.html) /

[, but it owns the shared transport state and knows how to multiplex multiple channels on a single backend (serial, CAN, middleware, …).](https://docs.rs/trait.CuSinkTask.html)

    channel: &'static [BridgeChannel](https://docs.rs/struct.BridgeChannel.html)<<Self::[Rx](https://docs.rs/trait.CuBridge.html#associatedtype.Rx) as [BridgeChannelSet](https://docs.rs/trait.BridgeChannelSet.html)>::[Id](https://docs.rs/trait.BridgeChannelSet.html#associatedtype.Id), Payload>,

) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [CuError](https://docs.rs/struct.CuError.html)>

#### fn [receive](https://docs.rs#tymethod.receive)<'a, Payload>(
    &mut self,
    ctx: &[CuContext](https://docs.rs/struct.CuContext.html),
    channel: &'static [BridgeChannel](https://docs.rs/struct.BridgeChannel.html)<<Self::[Rx](https://docs.rs/trait.CuBridge.html#associatedtype.Rx) as [BridgeChannelSet](https://docs.rs/trait.BridgeChannelSet.html)>::[Id](https://docs.rs/trait.BridgeChannelSet.html#associatedtype.Id), Payload>,
    msg: &mut [CuStampedData](https://docs.rs/struct.CuStampedData.html)<Payload, [CuMsgMetadata](https://docs.rs/struct.CuMsgMetadata.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [CuError](https://docs.rs/struct.CuError.html)>

Receives a message from the selected inbound channel.

Implementations should write into `msg` when data is available.

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

Called before the first send/receive cycle.

Gives the bridge a chance to prepare buffers before I/O.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*
